claims.statement: `schema.HARNESS_CONFIG_DIR` maps every harness name (claude, omp, opencode, antigravity, codex) to the same config directory `.claude`: recipes are authored against Claude's format, one Claude-canonical profile is emitted per (stack, harness), and no harness gets a re-authored variant — harnesses differ only in how they read the profile and reach hatago.

The harness is a run-time positional in a harness-first grammar (`harnessed container-run <harness> [path]`, same grammar on `host-run`), never a stack field; a stack may not be named after a harness (a name colliding with HARNESS_CONFIG_DIR is a schema error), and stack `harnesses:` is only a build-time convenience listing what `harnessed build <stack>` fans out to.

Anything accepting a harness name validates it against HARNESS_CONFIG_DIR at parse/load time — `_require_supported_harness` on the verbs, `_parse_hooks_skip_harnesses` for `hooks.skip_harnesses` (the same parser reused for `only_harnesses`), `_parse_harnesses` for stack `harnesses:` — so a typo like `ompp` fails with the list of valid names instead of silently doing nothing.

In the container mount set, the composed `.claude` config volume is mounted only for claude, omp and opencode — the three harnesses that read that tree — and the emitted `.mcp.json` is mounted only for claude; antigravity and codex receive only their harness-native identity files, mounted `:ro` only when present.

`HUB_TRANSPORT_EMITTED_HARNESSES` is exactly `{"claude"}`: only claude's hub wiring is emitted per stack, as `emit.write_mcp_json`'s `.mcp.json` naming the hatago entry (http url, or command/args under stdio) plus any `direct:` servers; a direct server named `hatago` is a schema error even in the all-direct branch, so a stack's validity never depends on a second recipe.

`_validate_direct_servers` and `_validate_hub_transport` fail the build when a non-claude harness is paired with a `direct:` server or `hub_transport: stdio`: the server would be excluded from hatago.config.json and absent from a config harnessed does not emit, so the recipe would read as configured while the harness never learned of it.

`container_run` re-validates the direct-server rule at launch (`_validate_direct_servers` on the launch-resolved server set) because the container path never assembles — an image built before a recipe gained `direct:` would otherwise come up silently toolless on a non-claude harness; CodeRabbit's suggested remedy of routing direct entries into omp's config was explicitly rejected as undoing the only-claude-emitted decision.

The launcher passes `HATAGO_TRANSPORT` explicitly from `Stack.hub_transport` (literal `none` when every server is direct) so emitter, launcher and entrypoint cannot disagree; the `harnessed-start` entrypoint starts the hub only when hatago.config.json is mounted AND transport is `http` — under `stdio` the harness spawns its own hub (which is what makes OAuth children authorizable), and under `none` no hub exists anywhere.

claude is the canonical native reader: the attach command is `claude --mcp-config '{mcp_cfg}'{strict}` where `{strict}` is ` --strict-mcp-config` by default so the emitted file is the only MCP source (written even with zero servers), and `--no-strict-mcp-config` drops the switch to opt back into the project's own `.mcp.json` and user config.

omp has no `--mcp-config` flag and reads MCP servers only from `~/.omp/agent/mcp.json`, so the container path generates a per-instance mcp.json (host file contents plus a `hatago` HTTP entry) and bind-mounts it ro OVER the rw agent-dir mount — the more-specific mount wins, so omp reaches hatago while the host's own mcp.json is never mutated, regenerated every launch so host edits propagate.

The omp image pre-installs the claude-hooks-bridge extension pinned `@drmikecrowe/omp-claude-hooks-bridge@0.5.0` into `~/.omp/plugins`; it maps Claude-shaped hooks onto omp's events only — no skills, commands or agents path — with 0.4.0 injecting SessionStart stdout / UserPromptSubmit context, 0.4.1 returning PreToolUse `updatedInput`, and 0.5.0 bridging PreCompact.

opencode natively reads `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md` and `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` but ignores `.mcp.json`; its MCP route is the image-baked `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` naming the hub. When a stack ships `instructions:`, the launcher's post-build `_merge_baked_opencode` reads the baked config, adds a persona agent and a `.claude/rules/*.md` glob, and writes the merged config into the profile where the mount set overrides the image path — carrying the baked `mcp.hatago` block verbatim. The agent name comes from `emit.opencode_agent_name(stack)`, shared by config key, prompt file and attach command.

antigravity (`agy`, gemini-cli-derived) reads `~/.gemini/`, not `.claude/`, consuming no Claude skills or commands; its MCP route is the baked global `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` with agy's `serverUrl` key pointing at the hub, and stack identity is delivered in agy's own shape (`.gemini/GEMINI.md` plus a fresh settings.json whose `context.fileName` is the absolute in-container identity path — written whole, unlike claude's merged settings floor). agy authenticates via Google OAuth into the OS keyring: the attach shell starts dbus + gnome-keyring inline and a persistent per-instance keyring store survives recreates (`--fresh` clears it).

codex 0.139+ speaks Streamable-HTTP natively, so its MCP route is the baked `~/.codex/config.toml` (`[mcp_servers.hatago] url`); it reads no Claude skills or commands and has no directory-rules primitive, so the assembler inlines identity plus every fanned `.claude/rules/*.md` into the one `.codex/AGENTS.md` — and because codex silently truncates at `project_doc_max_bytes` (32 KiB), the emitter truncates itself under the cap with a visible marker and warning.

The host backend's `_HOST_HARNESSES` record holds exactly claude (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) and omp (`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) today, each row pairing the config-dir env var (whose value IS the per-stack config/agent dir) with `argv0` and a `share_state` callable; materializing is deliberately not a record field because the two harnesses lay down different directory shapes, so `_host_launch_plan` branches once on harness.

A harness qualifies for host mode only if it exposes an env var whose value is a per-stack config/agent dir; codex, opencode and antigravity are absent because their rows are unestablished — no equivalent lever has been established — not because host mode is claude-shaped; adding one is filling in a row.

The host-run harness argument is spelled out rather than defaulted because `path` is the second positional: a defaulted harness would make `host-run .` bind `.` as the harness, so the grammar makes the harness lead (`harnessed host-run <harness> [path]`).

`share_state` is the host analog of the container bind-mounts, established per harness: claude symlinks `.credentials.json` (guarded against `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and with a replace-on-refresh rescue) and the session-state dirs, and copies the `.claude.json` account snapshot so onboarding is skipped without leaking writes back; omp symlinks `agent.db` (auth AND usage ledger), `history.db`, `sessions/`, `blobs/` and `memories/`, keeping config.yml, settings.json, RULES.md, APPEND_SYSTEM.md, mcp.json, managed-skills, terminal-sessions and models.db per-stack — and omp needs no credential rescue because SQLite rewrites `agent.db` in place, so its symlink never becomes a stale regular file.

`hostrun._HARNESS_CONFIG_DIR_ENV` pins each harness's own config-dir variables wherever catalog-authored content runs host-side (installs, setup scripts, the `setup.condition` eval), applied last: claude gets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the stack home, omp gets both `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` at the agent dir and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the nested bridge dir. Pinned rather than unset — an upstream installer honouring the var must land in the stack, and unsetting would send it to the user's real `$HOME/.claude` (measured: bd harnessed-8px.26 put 69 skills in an unrelated stack's home). `PI_CONFIG_DIR` is deliberately not listed because it is a name under $HOME, not a path.

Host omp writes identity WHOLE — `emit.render_omp_identity` renders `{filename: text}` for whichever of APPEND_SYSTEM.md/RULES.md the stack has content for, and the host materializer writes them without delimiter blocks, pruning or dedup, because under `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` the stack owns its agent dir (the whole file is its block); host launches assemble with `shared_identity=False` so nothing deposits blocks in the user's shared `~/.omp/agent`, while BOTH launch verbs still prune blocks of stacks that no longer resolve.

`_propagate_host_omp_config` seeds the per-stack `config.yml` from the host's live file on EVERY launch, gate or no gate — it is a function of the host's live state, not the recipe closure the fingerprint covers, and without it a host launch would run omp's shipped defaults (a factory reset, not isolation). Host keys win; only keys the fresh file does not define at all are carried over, so an install script's writes to `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/config.yml` are not silently undone — the same merge rule as claude's per-launch settings.json propagation, in YAML.

The claude-hooks bridge resolves hooks from `process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || ~/.claude`, so leaving the variable unset on host omp means the user's GLOBAL hooks fire inside a stack session while the stack's own never run — the inversion of the backend's isolation promise. A host omp launch therefore materializes a nested per-stack `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at `<agent dir>/claude-config` and exports it at the exec; settings.json is the only file the bridge reads and the one file in that dir propagated every launch, gated or not; it is nested (not a sibling) so `host-gc` does not see a phantom harness, and deliberately distinct from `host_home(stack, "claude")` — no claude `seed_auth` runs on the omp path because omp authenticates out of `agent.db`.

Claude-shaped `skills:` are inert on host omp — the bridge covers command hooks only and omp's own skill surface is a format harnessed does not emit, so the skills land in the profile read by nothing — and the gap is stated at launch by `_note_host_omp_skill_gap` in the `[INFO]` register rather than encoded in `capmatrix`, whose axis is the backend; hooks are NOT part of the gap (delivered via the bridge and nested `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), and the remedy the message names is running the stack under `container-run`.

Host mode has no hatago hub: `HostBackend.wire_mcp` uses `_host_native_mcp` to resolve the stack's servers natively (claude spawns stdio children itself and connects url servers directly; service-backed servers are warned and skipped), and the MCP file is ALWAYS written even with zero servers because writing it is the isolation — claude gets `<home>/.mcp.json` + `--strict-mcp-config`, omp gets `<agent dir>/mcp.json` unconditionally (the per-stack agent dir is what strict buys on the claude path), and `--no-strict-mcp-config` for omp is accepted-and-inert, reported at launch.

`attachcmd.py` derives the attach command from `_HARNESS_ATTACH_CMD` (claude `--mcp-config`+`{strict}`, plain `omp`/`opencode`/`codex`, `agy` for antigravity) with omp and opencode overridden in code — omp pins its session dir, opencode appends `--agent <name>` only when a persona was baked (i.e. the stack ships `instructions:`); `_attach` composes one `bash -l -c` line (mise trust -a, the Model A init prologue, the antigravity keyring prefix if any, then the harness tail) exec'd via `podman exec -it -w <start_dir>`, appending the `--` passthrough shell-quoted except under `--shell`.

omp keys a folder's session dir from the cwd relative to `$HOME`, so inside the pod — where `$HOME` is `/home/harnessed` but the cwd is the mirrored host path — omp escapes the key and `/resume` finds nothing; `_omp_attach_cmd` recomputes the key against the HOST home (`-` + path relative to `$HOME`, slashes folded to dashes; the full path when the project sits outside the host home) and pins it via `--session-dir`. The dir is fixed at attach time — `cd` elsewhere does not re-key the picker — which is what lets aoe dashboard relaunches resume the right per-folder session: the replayed launch re-derives the same start directory, so the same pinned key resolves.

A second, narrower omp seed shadows `config.yml` only when the host's file still names the retired local-dev bridge path: `_omp_config_seed_mount` mounts a per-instance copy with just that obsolete `extensions` entry removed, so inside the pod the `~`-relative path cannot both warn about a missing module and double-load the image-installed plugin.
